title: What If the Sahara Turned Green Again?

scenes.text: What if the Sahara turned green again? It already has, and not that long ago.
Roughly eleven thousand to five thousand years ago, grass and shrubs covered about nine million square kilometres of North Africa.
Rainfall was about ten times today's, filling dry basins with lakes where hippos, elephants and antelope lived.
Then, about five thousand years ago, it dried out. The switch back to desert took only around two hundred years.
The cause is Earth's wobble. A cycle of about twenty-three thousand years shifts summer sunlight, strengthening or weakening Africa's monsoon.
The next sunlight peak is roughly ten thousand years away, though some model studies suggest greenhouse gases could bring greening sooner.

description:
What if the Sahara turned green again?
It was green from roughly 11,000 to 5,000 years ago, with lakes and hippos, driven by a 23,000-year orbital cycle. The next peak is about 10,000 years away.
